title: King Oliver's playing and his gum and teeth trouble
summary: Oliver played as he had for years but his bridge failed from pyorrhea, so he did not play for about a month in 1933-34 and was not playing well afterward.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Some other things I'd like to know about King Oliver. How well was he playing when you joined, and then how did it progress as the two years went on?
He was playing just like he had been playing for years. Real good and (?) and pretty. He didn't play as high as Louis, but he played up around D and E.
Although he influenced Louis at one time, obviously, do you think there's any chance that maybe he was starting to listen to Louis in later years? Learn from the guy who he taught?

I don't know whether he would do that or not. Because he was kind of for himself, you know what I mean? Louis would tell everybody that this is the man that I adore, is King Oliver. He always did that say. He said, King gave me my break and he learnt me a lot of things. So I don't
know... But see, at that time, too, he was kind of getting kind of disgusted. His teeth was bothering him, you know. He had pyorrhea. When he got the teeth, they never fitted right.
Did he have new teeth by the time you joined, or was that later?
Oh, his teeth started giving him trouble when I was in the band.
He already had false teeth at that time?

Yeah. He might have had a bridge in there, and then the ones he had a bridge on, he got pyorrhea around them, and they gave out, so his bridge came out. For a little while there, maybe a month or more, he didn't play.
In 1933. In '33 and '34, he didn't play, because he was waiting to get his teeth fixed.
That was for a month, you said.
About a month or so, or maybe six weeks or something like that.
So as it went on into '34, after he did get it fixed, how was playing then?
